note: A baseline is a configured, versioned artefact. This file is the pin: the runner reads the tool's own version at run time, compares it against `accepted`, and refuses to publish a row on a version that is not on the list. A drifted version is not a regression, it is a different baseline — so the honest outcome is a refusal with the observed version named, not a row with an asterisk. `--exploratory` still runs it and marks the row `pin_satisfied: false`.

baselines.title: Native filesystem (copy-per-version)
baselines.version_source: platform.filesystem and platform.os_version of the row — the baseline is the host filesystem itself, which has no separate version string
baselines.terms: No third-party terms. The host's own filesystem.

baselines.title: Git worktrees
baselines.terms: GPL-2.0-only. Publishing measurements of Git carries no restriction; Git imposes no benchmark-publication term.

baselines.title: Folder replication (rsync)
baselines.terms: GPL-3.0-or-later. No benchmark-publication restriction. Syncthing (MPL-2.0) is the other member of this family and is equally publishable; it is not implemented here because it needs two live daemons and a network, which is a different runner.

competitor_products.reason: Dropbox Terms of Service §Acceptable Use prohibits publishing benchmark results without written consent. No consent has been sought, so no runner exists and no number may be quoted — including from a third-party blog post.
Google APIs Terms of Service §3(d) prohibits publishing benchmarks of the services without prior written consent. Same conclusion.
The Perforce end-user licence agreement prohibits disclosure of benchmark or performance results. Same conclusion.
